guides.title: Print a PDF or a web page
steps: Open the PDF or the web page you want on paper.
Press the Ctrl key and the P key together. A Print window opens.
Look at the Printer box. Make sure it shows your usual printer. Click the box to pick another one.
To print only some pages, click Pages and type the page numbers, like 1-2.
Click the blue Print button.
Nothing came out? Close this guide and click 'Fix my printer' on the main screen.

guides.title: Scan a document
steps: Put the paper face down on the glass of your scanner, or face up in the feeder on top. Close the lid.
Click the Start button, type Scan, and open the app called Scan or Windows Scan. (Or use the scan button on your printer.)
Pick your scanner from the Scanner box.
Under File type choose PDF for papers, or JPG for photos.
Click Preview to check that the page looks right. Click Scan when it does.
When it finishes, click View. The scanned file is saved in your Documents folder, in a folder called Scanned Documents.
Tip: to email it, see the guide 'Attach a photo to an email'. It works the same way for PDFs.

guides.title: Attach a photo to an email
steps: Start a new email, or open the email you are replying to.
Look for a paper clip picture at the top of the email window. Click it. If you see the word Attach, click that.
Choose 'Browse this computer' or 'Attach file' if it asks.
Click Pictures on the left side, or the folder where your photo is saved.
Click the photo once to pick it. To pick more than one, hold the Ctrl key and click each one.
Click Open. The photo name appears in your email.
Check that the photo name is showing, then click Send.

guides.title: Take a screenshot and send it to Trey
steps: Get the problem on your screen, so Trey can see what you see.
Press the Windows key, the Shift key and the S key all together. The screen turns gray and a small bar appears at the top.
Click and hold the mouse button, drag a box over the part you want to show, then let go.
The picture is now saved in the computer's memory. A small message shows in the bottom right corner.
Start a new email to Trey. Type Trey's email address in the To box.
Click in the big white message area, then press the Ctrl key and the V key together. The picture appears.
Add a few words about what is wrong, then click Send.

guides.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
steps: Look at the bottom right corner of the screen, near the clock. Click the little globe or Wi-Fi picture.
A list of Wi-Fi names opens. Click the name of your home Wi-Fi.
Make sure 'Connect automatically' is ticked, then click Connect.
Type the Wi-Fi password. It is usually on a sticker on the back or bottom of your internet box (router).
Click Next. In a few seconds it should say Connected.
Still not working? Close this guide and click 'Fix my internet' on the main screen.

guides.title: Join a Zoom or video call
steps: Open the email or message with the meeting invite.
Click the blue link that says Join, or the long link that starts with https. Your web browser opens.
If it asks 'Open Zoom Meetings?' click Open. If it asks to download Zoom, click Download and open the file.
Type your name if it asks, then click Join.
If it asks about the computer audio, click 'Join with Computer Audio'.
Make sure the microphone and camera pictures at the bottom left have no red line through them. Click them to turn them on or off.
To leave, click the red Leave button at the bottom right.
No sound or picture? Close this guide and click 'Fix sound/mic/camera' on the main screen.

guides.title: Save a photo from an email
steps: Open the email that has the photo in it.
Right-click on the photo (press the right mouse button). A small menu opens.
Click 'Save as' or 'Save picture as'. If you do not see that, look for 'Download' under the photo.
Click Pictures on the left side so you will know where it is later.
Click Save.
To find it later, open File Explorer (the yellow folder at the bottom of the screen) and click Pictures.

guides.title: Make text bigger in my browser or email
steps: In your browser or email, press and hold the Ctrl key.
While holding it, press the plus key (+) a few times. Each press makes everything a little bigger.
Or hold Ctrl and roll the wheel on your mouse forward.
To make it smaller again, hold Ctrl and press the minus key (-).
To put it back to normal, hold Ctrl and press the zero key (0).
To make the whole computer bigger, use the 'Big text' switch on the left side of this window.

guides.title: Find something I downloaded
steps: Open File Explorer. It is the yellow folder picture at the bottom of the screen.
Click Downloads on the left side.
The newest files are at the top. Look at the dates on the right.
Double-click a file to open it.
Tip: you can also click 'My files' on the left side of this window and type part of the name.
Do not open a download you do not remember. If it came from a pop-up or an email you do not trust, click the red scary pop-up button instead.

guides.title: Spot a scam email or text
steps: A real company will not scare you or rush you. Be careful if a message says 'act now', 'your account is locked', 'you won', or 'you owe money'.
Never call a phone number that is in an email, text or pop-up. Look the number up yourself on a real bill or card.
Look at who sent it. Scam emails often come from strange addresses, with spelling mistakes or a name that does not match.
Do not click links or open attachments you did not expect. Gift cards, wire transfers and remote-control programs are always a scam if someone asks for them.
Do not give out passwords, bank details or codes that come in a text message. Real companies never ask you for these.
Not sure? Do not reply. Click 'Send Trey a report' or phone Trey and ask him first.
If you already clicked something, turn off the Wi-Fi and use the red scary pop-up button.
